doc.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Basie's writers and his formula
summary: Fuller names Sammy Nestico and Neal Hefti as Basie writers, and how Freddie Green refused his own chart with altered chords.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who were the principal writers at that point?
The writers were Sammy Nestico, and the one before him… he wasn’t writing that much when I get in the band. His stuff was already in the book.
So it was like the second testament band?
Yes, but he wanted some white writers because he wanted the band to be accepted with the white audience.

Neal Hefti, exactly. He sang a couple things to me to let me know where Reed was coming from. I wrote something for the band and Freddie Green looked at this and said he won’t play this. So you’ve got all those flat sevenths and raised ninths and Basie is simple, C7, G7. He didn’t want to put that up there. He didn’t like that.

So he had a very strong concept of what he wanted musically because it was a successful formula and he knew what he was catering to and where he was taking the audience, he wanted to take the band too.
